title: Dynamic reservation lane and approval rubric for SLA-backed throughput
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Dedicated capacity often need a mix of steady reserved throughput and temporary burst lanes (for launches, seasonal traffic). Current intake funnels all requests through a single approval path which increases cycle time for straightforward low-risk requests and makes it hard to reason about SLA-backed throughput that must be guaranteed in contract.

Goal: Define a lightweight, auditable reservation intake that classifies requests into dynamic lanes (steady, burst, probationary) and applies an approval rubric that ties SLA throughput guarantees to: capacity scoring, autoscaling policy templates, cost estimate, and billing/accounting tags. Deliverables: intake form schema, lane selection logic, approval rubric/checklist, preflight simulation step, and integration points for Console and billing metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form schema implemented with fields for expected p50/p95 throughput, peak QPS window, duration of sustained throughput, and desired SLA tier
Automated lane classification returns one of: steady-reserve, burst-credit, probationary-trial with rationale string
Approval rubric checklist implemented (risk score, capacity available, cost delta, security/compliance check) and surfaced to approvers in Console
Preflight simulator can run a traffic profile against historical fleet utilization and return probability-of-violation metric
Activation path tags reservation with billing dimensions and hooks autoscaling policy template to fleet controls
steps: 1) Intake UI + API: requester provides workload profile (expected tpm, 95th latency target, window), intent (launch, steady-state, seasonal), contract SLO
2) Scoring: run request through capacity scorer (utilization forecast + buffer) to produce capacity_needed and risk_score
3) Lane assignment: map score and intent to lane: steady-reserve | burst-credit | probationary-trial
4) Approval checklist generation: produce checklist items (fleet availability, cross-customer impact, cost estimate, legal/compliance flags) for approver review
5) Preflight simulation: optional stage that simulates the requested traffic profile against current committed and free fleet to estimate P(violation) and identify fallback options
6) Approver action: Approve / Request changes / Escalate to capacity council (with editable buffer and billing terms)
7) Activation: create reservation in provisioning system, attach autoscaling template, set rollout window and observability hooks
8) Post-activation: create dashboard link in Console, cost allocation tags, and retention of preflight report for audits
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Decided to adopt three lanes (steady-reserve, burst-credit, probationary-trial) to balance speed and risk
2026-02-25: Chose capacity scorer approach combining short-term utilization forecast + configurable safety buffer; ENG to prototype model
2026-03-01: Approval rubric will include mandatory cost delta and billing tags; Finance approved minimal tag set
2026-03-03: Agreed preflight simulation is optional but recommended for P1/P0 requests and must run in < 30s for UX flow
updates: 2026-02-20 Sofia Patel: Drafted initial PRD and lane definitions; added stakeholders and proposed field set for intake form (link in artifacts)
2026-02-24 Marcus Chen: Engineering spike started to prototype capacity scorer; created ENG spike ticket ENG-19845; initial model uses 7-day window and 95th percentile baseline
2026-02-28 Priya Rao: Infra confirms tagging and billing dimensions available via billing-v2; will expose autoscale template bindings by 2026-03-12
2026-03-02 Marcus Chen: Prototype preflight simulator returns synthetic risk score; pushed draft PR with simulator harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/pull/412
2026-03-05 Sofia Patel: Product review with Finance and SRE; updated acceptance criteria to require simulation P(violation) output and approver rationale field
notes: Edge cases: multi-region reservations require additional gating; plan to add secondary approval flag for cross-region SLA guarantees
Rollout plan: start with internal beta for two strategic customers, then open to small enterprise cohort before GA
Metrics to monitor post-GA: mean time to approve, fraction of reservations needing manual escalation, realized P(violation) vs predicted
